This confirms the exact scenario: the same `reader` object is reused in a `for` loop across all update sites, calling `read()` once per site. Since `filesFromThisSite` isn't cleared between calls, files accumulate from the first site and are never cleared, so `filesFromThisSite.contains(file)` incorrectly returns true for a file added by a previous site — causing that logic branch to treat cross-site files as belonging to "this site" and preventing the shadowing/overriding branch from executing.

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit adds `filesFromThisSite.clear();` at the start of `XMLFileReader.read()`. I traced the history of `filesFromThisSite` in `XMLFileReader.java` using `git log -S "filesFromThisSite"`, which showed it was introduced in exactly one prior commit (`34d01ebe9`) besides the fix itself. I then inspected that commit's full diff and checked how `XMLFileReader` instances are used elsewhere in the codebase (`XMLFileDownloader.java`).

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `34d01ebe9` ("Updater: prefer the update site's current versions to locally-cached ones") introduced the field `protected Set<FileObject> filesFromThisSite = new HashSet<FileObject>();`, initialized only once at declaration, and replaced the previous per-call check `(updateSite != null && updateSite.equals(file.updateSite)) || (updateSite == null && file.updateSite == null)` with a check against this persistent set: `filesFromThisSite.contains(file)`. Because the set is never cleared, it accumulates `FileObject`s across every call to `read()` on the same `XMLFileReader` instance.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** In `XMLFileDownloader.java` (`start()` method), a single `XMLFileReader reader` instance is created once and then `reader.read(name, in, updateSite.timestamp)` is called repeatedly inside a `for` loop over all configured update sites. This means `filesFromThisSite` retains entries from earlier sites when processing later sites, so `filesFromThisSite.contains(file)` can spuriously return `true` for files that actually belong to a different (earlier) site. This routes execution into the "same site, just update the object" branch instead of the branch that handles cross-site overriding/shadowing (rank comparison, `overriddenUpdateSites` tracking, warnings), which matches the bug description exactly ("would prevent any shadowing"). The one-line fix (`filesFromThisSite.clear();` at the top of `read()`) directly patches this omission, confirming that the missing clear in `34d01ebe9` is the root cause.

I'm confident in this identification — the fix is a single-line addition that directly addresses a set that was added but never cleared, and the commit that added the set is the only candidate found via `git log -S`.
